title: Observation
description:
One normalised record of one thing an agent did, from any host.

An observation is a PROFILE of journal-event.schema.json, not a replacement for it. The upstream schema already carries `phase`, `tokens`, `cost_usd`, `injected_units`, the hash chain, and additionalProperties:true for host-native passthrough; decision S5 forbids forking it. This document adds exactly one required thing - the `source` block - and constrains the corners of `payload` that Witness assigns meaning to.

The upstream copy is vendored under schemas/vendor/ and pinned. It is never edited here.

allOf.$comment: Everything upstream requires - audit_id, session_id, timestamp, event, actor, trace_id - is required here too. An observation that does not satisfy the journal-event contract is not an observation.

payload.description: Upstream leaves this open. The three properties below are the only ones Witness assigns meaning to; an adapter may add host-native keys alongside them and they will be carried through unchanged.

corroborated_by.description:
Other sources that independently reported a consistent value, as `host:channel` pairs.

RECORDING CORROBORATION NEVER CHANGES `source.tier` (decision S3, SPEC.md section 4.4). Finding a matching value in a host audit log does not make a locally-captured value host-attested; only a tier B source that carries the value itself can do that. This rule will feel wrong the first time it makes a demo look weaker than it 'really' is - that pressure is precisely why it is written down.

error.description: Required whenever any entry in `unavailable` is `collection_failed`. The distinction between 'the host has no such field' and 'we failed to read it' is the difference between a limit and a bug, and an auditor is entitled to know which they are looking at.
